title: Hard Stop
intro: You can't cut what you can't stop, and stopping costs far more than going. This one is hard on your legs, and it brakes sideways, which is how you stop when you're pulled wide. It's twenty stops, seventeen at full speed, each with its own rest, and no run-in is longer than ten metres. Do Landing Gear first if you haven't, because a brake is a landing you have to hold.

You need a court or about twenty-five metres of flat ground with real grip, and court shoes. A slick surface is where an ankle goes. Mark each distance with tape or a line, not cones or bags you could step on. Sore thighs and glutes for a few days is normal. Do it on fresh legs at the start of a training day. If a stop gets longer, wider or lazier, or your legs feel slow and heavy, end the session there.

before.label: Not today
before.text: A sore ankle, knee, calf, hamstring, groin or Achilles, or an injury in the last month? Get it looked at first.

before.label: Stop and get it checked
before.text: A sharp pain, pain that spreads, numbness, swelling, a joint that gives way, or a sudden pull or pop.

before.label: Stop now
before.text: Chest pain, dizziness, a heartbeat that races or skips, or breathing that doesn't feel right. Get it looked at before you train again. Told to be careful with hard exercise? Check with your doctor first.

before.label: A day or two later
before.text: Far more sore than normal, or your pee goes dark? Get it checked the same day.

before.label: Past injury
before.text: Ever torn a knee ligament, or coming back from an ankle injury? Ask whoever treated you if hard stops and cuts are OK.

before.label: Keep clear
before.text: Wait until the soreness has gone, and never less than 48 hours, before another hard running session or heavy leg lifting. Keep it two days clear of a match, before and after.

before.label: First time
before.text: Do half the reps in the last two blocks and take the full rest.

exercises.name: Lateral Run to Outside-Leg Stop
exercises.note: Alternate sides. Do the first two at about three-quarter speed, then go flat out.
